newsitem.title: UK: Moody's says B3 rating reflects Bulgaria's debt.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says B3 rating reflects Bulgaria's debt.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday that Bulgaria's slow progress and heavy debt burden were shown in its B3 sovereign ceiling rating.

"Bulgaria's B3 sovereign ceiling for bonds and Caa ceiling for bank deposits reflect the difficulties the country faces in meeting its relatively onerous foreign currency obligations as well as the slow pace of enterprise restructuring, which has been hindering macroeconomic stabilisation," Moody's said in a statement.
The agency said Bulgaria was currently dependent on credit from multilateral agencies to meet its external debt service payments -- estimated at $1.2 billion for 1997 by Moody's.

"The IMF, however, has postponed the disbursement of the second tranche of the stand-by credit facility, because of the slow progress on enterprise reform," Moody's said. "In the absence of other sources of funding, access to external credit depends on the country's adherence to the stringent structural reform measures required by the supranational agencies."
"Only this course of action would prevent a default, put the economy on a sustainable growth path, and open up other sources of financing in the medium term," Moody's said.
Moody's concluded that the speed and success of structural reforms would be a major determinant of the nation's credit quality in the future.
